newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes higher on technical recovery.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes higher on technical recovery.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on a technical recovery tied to signals the market was oversold with commercial buying in the December also cited, traders said.

Technical indicators showed the market was oversold with the nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for July at 15 percent as of midsession and that month's RSI closed at 24 percent. An RSI of 30 or less is considered an oversold market. Corn early this week fell to new-two year lows.
Talk circulated that several private forecasters were citing potentially drier weather in the Midwest soon.
But little new feature was noted with recent U.S. Midwest weather nearly perfect for crop development and only routine exports have been noted.
Commercial buying in the December led to talk Japan may be pricing some of their new crop corn import needs.
Cargill Inc, Term Commodities, Farmers Commodities and Continental Grain were noted buyers of December, traders said. Term was a noted purchaser of 1,000 December $2.30 corn calls, traders said.
Corn closed 2-1/2 cents per bushel higher to 1-1/2 lower, with July up 2-1/2 at $2.45-3/4.

Cargill Inc bought two million bushels of December, Term Commoditeirs bought 3.5 million December and Continental Grain plus Farmers Commodities each bought one million bushels of December, traders said.
Griffin Trading sold 20 million bushels of December and Cargill Inc sold 6.5 million bushels of July, traders said.
In spread trading, Cargill Inc did four million September/July at 10 to 11 cents, premium July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 67,000 contracts, below the 68,950 traded Tuesday.

In corn options, LIT America bought 600 September $2.50 calls at 3-3/4 to 3-7/8 cents, Griffin Trading sold 500 September $2.40 calls at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 cents and Term Commodities, the marketing arm for Louis Dreyfus Corp, bought 1,000 December $2.30 calls at 13 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, up from the 14,694 traded Tuesday.
